items.title: Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy
items.desc: Since May, SpaceXSI has been renting compute to competitors like Anthropic and Google while scaling back its own AI projects. Anthropic pays about $3.1 billion a month, Google $800 million, the New York Times reports. After its June IPO, SpaceXSI disbanded the 60-person Grok Imagine team, among other cuts. The article Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Anthropic's massive compute needs align with growing profit pressure at xAI, Elon Musk's AI unit. xAI has rented compute to rivals since May, and its June IPO made the push for revenue even more urgent, the New York Times reports . Anthropic is now xAI's biggest customer with a contract worth roughly $3.1 billion a month. Google spends $800 million. Either deal can be canceled with 90 days' notice. xAI now accounts for over half of xAI's total revenue. Insiders say the company had to finish new data centers by October to fill Anthropic's orders, and Musk says the Claude maker wants to rent even more. In August, Musk pushed engineers in a group chat for "revenue per GPU," frustrated in part that xAI's own models can barely compete. He reportedly renamed an internal chat "Sell compute because we can't compete." Ad xAI is cutting or restructuring its own AI projects to match that shift. Unit chief Mike Nicolls told staff in November that the 60-person team behind the Grok Imagine image and video generator would be disbanded. An internal memo pointed to critical business priorities. xAI shut down its AI avatars in September, and OpenAI also killed its Sora video model over capacity limits. Ad Already a subscriber? items.title: Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles
items.desc: Chinese military researchers fear that AI advances could give the US an edge in the nuclear balance of power. The article Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Chinese military researchers fear that AI advances could give the US an edge in the nuclear balance of power. Experts in China worry that artificial intelligence could make it easier for US forces to detect and destroy Chinese nuclear missiles, according to a New York Times analysis. That would undermine China's deterrence strategy, which relies on a guaranteed second-strike capability. Researchers at the Academy of Military Sciences in Beijing write that AI could shrink US decision-making time from 15 to 30 minutes down to 90 seconds. China currently has about 620 operational warheads, according to the Federation of American Scientists, and is expected to expand its arsenal to roughly 1,000 by 2030. At the same time, Chinese military institutes are studying how AI could make their own weapons harder to intercept, for instance by using AI-controlled flight paths for hypersonic missiles. Experts warn, however, that flawed AI data could trigger dangerous miscalculations during a crisis. That risk proved very real earlier this year, when the US military nearly boarded a Chinese ship based on a false, AI-generated intelligence report . Xi Jinping did discuss nuclear risks at a summit with Trump and Putin, but AI's role in nuclear weapons never came up, according to the report. Despite the growing urgency, the US and China have made almost no progress on talks about AI safeguards in nuclear systems. Ad Ad Already a subscriber? Sign in

items.title: Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks
items.desc: Nvidia's board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. The article Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Nvidia's board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. The decision was unanimous, Nvidia said in a press release, following talks with Huang and feedback from senior US government officials who concluded that his return poses no national security risk. CFO Colette Kress had been running the company on an interim basis , and the stock had tanked during that period. President Donald J. Trump praised the decision on Truth Social, saying the US Attorney General found no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang. The move comes after reports that Huang had been targeted by foreign intelligence operations . An independent board committee is still investigating the matter with outside counsel. The US government is also reviewing Nvidia's business dealings. Trump urged the company to keep looking into whether its export control compliance holds up. Nvidia has already set up a dedicated oversight committee for that purpose and is searching for a Chief Compliance Officer. Huang and the company said they'll continue cooperating with authorities and internal investigators. Nvidia's stock jumped more than 30 percent on the news. Ad Ad Already a subscriber? Sign in

items.title: Using Fallbacks for a Robust Front-End
items.desc: It’s important to use fallbacks to build a robust front end, either to quietly and discreetly avoid the error or to communicate it to our users. Using Fallbacks for a Robust Front-End originally handwritten and published with love on CSS-Tricks . You should really get the newsletter as well.
items.full: NVIDIA L4 GPUs. 5-second cold starts. Scale to zero when idle. Anyone who has been working in web development for a while will be familiar with this now-legendary meme from xkcd . It illustrates just how fragile the technical infrastructure of a website or app can be. That’s why it’s important to use fallbacks to build a robust front end, either to quietly and discreetly avoid the error or to communicate it to our users. The issue of robustness is so important that it is actually one of the four principles of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) ! So how can we provide a modern front end without excluding users who use browsers and hardware that are only partially compatible or not compatible at all? The answer lies in implementing multiple safety nets in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, so that we are prepared for the worst-case scenario and can provide our users with the best possible experience. Two distinctions The main difference between the use of fallbacks and progressive enhancement lies in the directions in which the two approaches aim. While progressive enhancement is about automatically making certain features available as long as they are supported (forward), fallbacks are about what happens when something is not available or accessible (backward). For example, we can offer a shiny new CSS feature that makes interacting with our website even more enjoyable. But if this feature isn’t available in some browsers, no one will notice, because a version that’s supported by older browsers is available instead. Progressive enhancement in action! Another example: If JavaScript cannot be loaded for a critical application, we provide a fallback that either offers basic functionality or, at the very least, displays a message explaining what the problem is. While one doesn’t necessarily exclude the other, their approaches are quite different. My personal recommendation is to always work with progressive enhancement as a guiding principle and to consider fallbacks whenever possible. Web platform: Staying up-to-date with the web platform To evaluate new features intended for production, we must first determine the extent to which a feature is supported. Since 2023, the Interop project has been in place, in which major browser vendors collaborate to release new features for the web platform more or less simultaneously. This serves as a general overview. Related to this is the Baseline project, which shows, for specific features, the extent to which they are supported and how long they have been available. However, it is extremely important to note that it does not track browser support for accessibility features built into the web platform! Another important resource for checking compatibility is Can I Use . Here, you can get a quick overview of browser support for various features. HTML: Error pages and <noscript> Let’s start with the foundation of the World Wide Web: HTML. Modern tech stacks place a strong emphasis on client-side rendered JavaScript, which can offer many benefits to users in more complex applications. items.title: Meta's Alexandr Wang warns the AI industry isn't ready for what's coming after Riemann breakthrough
items.desc: Meta's Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang sees the recent AI-assisted proof sketch of the Riemann Hypothesis as a clear sign that superintelligence is right around the corner. The article Meta's Alexandr Wang warns the AI industry isn't ready for what's coming after Riemann breakthrough appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Meta's Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang sees the recent AI-assisted proof sketch of the Riemann Hypothesis as a clear sign that superintelligence is right around the corner. The Riemann Hypothesis is widely considered the most intellectually demanding unsolved problem in mathematics. The brightest minds have failed to crack it for 150 years. The fact that an AI model played a major role in the breakthrough shows that raw intelligence is no longer the bottleneck, Wang argues. According to Wang, current models only lack domain-specific knowledge and practical infrastructure to outperform humans in nearly every field. That includes AI research itself. Since AI research is intellectually less demanding than the Riemann Hypothesis, Wang believes models could soon automate their own development and improve themselves. They could also dramatically speed up biological research, weapons research, and economic research at a pace humans can barely follow. Wang also warns that the AI industry isn't thinking hard enough about what comes next. In his view, many in the field treat superintelligence as inevitable and focus only on safety. But the stakes are much broader than that, he argues. The industry needs to actively ensure that AI gives people more agency rather than taking control of society. That would require a sharp departure from the current course, Wang says. Despite having its own superintelligence team , Meta isn't a major player at the frontier right now. items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra solved a math theorem no other AI could crack, then invented its own proof strategy
items.desc: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra independently produced a machine-verifiable Lean proof of Smoktunowicz's gap theorem, the first of its kind according to Vals AI. The model chose its own approach because key foundations were missing from Mathlib. On Autoform-Hard, Astra now leads the leaderboard with 49 of 56 tasks solved. The article GPT-6.2 Astra solved a math theorem no other AI could crack, then invented its own proof strategy appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra produced a formalized, machine-verifiable proof of a 2006 theorem with zero human help during the run. According to Vals AI , it's the first known proof of Smoktunowicz's gap theorem written in Lean . The theorem states that when a mathematical system multiplies its basic building blocks, growth is either quite slow or very fast. There's no middle ground. Because key foundations of the original proof were missing from the math library Mathlib, Astra took a different route than the published mathematical proofs , Vals says. It used "capacity," a metric from existing research that checks the minimum number of elements added per computation step. This happened on Autoform-Hard , a subset of Meta FAIR's AutoformBench curated by Vals. It contains 56 tasks (five corrected) that ten models in Meta's study failed to solve within budget. When Astra tried to quit after 47 minutes and eight dollars, the system rejected the attempt since unsolved submissions aren't accepted until $20 has been spent. After nine minutes of silence with no code input while it searched for a new strategy, Astra delivered the 1,800-line proof at the 94-minute mark for $21.58. It now leads the leaderboard with 49 solved tasks, ahead of GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Fable 5.2 at 48 each. Already a subscriber? Sign in

items.title: Symphony Review: A Team of AI Agents for the Business Behind Your Website
items.desc: You can keep your WordPress site in good shape yet still lose leads to unanswered emails, missed follow-ups, and an out-of-date calendar. My Symphony review looks at a team of AI agents, led by one orchestrator, that can organize your work and wait for approval. The post " Symphony Review: A Team of AI Agents for the Business Behind Your Website " first appeared on WP Mayor .
items.full: To be a small business owner is to spin multiple plates at once: lead generation, client outreach, general marketing and sales, design, and much more. Often, some of those plates will fall and smash, which might mean you lose a good prospect, don’t hit a deadline, or myriad other negatives. By the end of this Symphony review, you might choose to take a breath and let its Maestro orchestrator organize your work tasks, so you can sweep up the broken crockery! Each of Symphony’s four pricing tiers comes with the core functionality of Maestro and the ability to use multiple AI agents around the clock. The difference between each plan is the number of AI credits you receive per month, the ‘activity level’ of your agents, the number of actions you have available, and your usage allocation. Here are the three premium plans: The cost I give here is based on annual billing. A month-by-month subscription costs slightly more. There aren’t any exact figures on the activity level of your agents and usage allocation either, just that higher tiers give you more. Free is more of an extended taster of what Symphony can give you. There’s an allocation of 500 credits per month and 100 daily credits. I think the Free plan is a generous offering given what’s included in the premium tiers. You also get two agent actions and briefings. If your credits run out before the month’s end, agents pause the work and wait for your credit allocation. It means you won’t need to adapt to an unfinished workflow or lose any work. If you run a small business, there are a few concerns you likely have regularly: This is what Symphony aims to improve. In a nutshell, you chat with Maestro (the orchestrator) and after it learns about your business, it dishes out the work to a set of AI agents. Each agent has one area of responsibility, but you can add custom agents if you need to work on a specific task. Wix claims the agent knowledge comes from 300 million businesses across a variety of regions and industries. Symphony is platform-agnostic , which means you don’t need to run a Wix site to use it (although you do need a Wix account). Instead, it connects to your calendars, email account, CRM, MCP server, and other tools. My first impression is that Symphony is going to be most helpful for single-person businesses or small teams. Freelancers or content creators fit the bill, but agencies that run several projects at once can also benefit. The Pro plan is likely the best fit for all of these business types. A freelancer with a small workload could opt for Basic, but you wouldn’t want to restrict your growth based on your Symphony plan. There are four core aspects to Symphony that cover the majority of your needs: Everything works through human-language prompts , and each project gets its own contained workspace. For instance, you can tell Maestro the details of your business and it assembles a team of AI agents based on the suitability for the task. It covers outreach and marketing, scheduling, research, design, and even finance. The information is also used to build a knowledge base, which involves a constant learning cycle. items.title: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits
items.desc: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has released internal perplexity scores for the entire GPT series for the first time, up to an unreleased model beyond the current generation. The metric shows that core capabilities emerge at surprisingly precise thresholds. Pachocki is pushing to make perplexity an industry-wide progress metric and establish shared limits before control over AI behavior erodes. The article OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI ties capabilities like fluent conversation and math breakthroughs to specific scores. For the first time, chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is showing where the GPT series sits on that scale, up to an unreleased model beyond GPT-6. Pachocki wants to make perplexity a common measure of progress for the AI industry and published internal scores for the GPT series in a bl o g post . The metric has long been standard in AI research and Transformer development because it reliably measures how well a pretrained base model predicts the next token in a text. Lower scores mean more accurate predictions. A perplexity of 2 roughly means the model is as uncertain about the next token as if it were choosing between two equally likely options. Before it stopped publishing openly, OpenAI often released perplexity scores to show how its models were improving. Releasing them again is a trade-off, Pachocki writes . While rivals get a clearer picture of where OpenAI stands, he says, the need for shared safety standards outweighs that downside. He hopes for a common scientific foundation that lets labs coordinate their pace of development at critical points. Pachocki says many capabilities of modern models map surprisingly closely to specific perplexity scores, even though it wasn't clear beforehand that they would appear at those thresholds. He reports the figures on a logarithmic scale called log-perplexity, where lower scores are still better. In his account, GPT-3.5 first enabled fluent conversation at around 0.99, laying the groundwork for the original ChatGPT. At about 0.91, GPT-4 unlocked productive chain-of-thought reasoning, or working through problems step by step. Below 0.8, he writes, transformative capabilities emerged in cybersecurity and math . The published chart plots OpenAI's base-model log-perplexity by release or evaluation date through November 2026. It covers GPT-5 , GPT-5.1 , GPT-5.2 , GPT-5.3-Codex , GPT-5.4 , GPT-5.5 , GPT-5.6 Sol , GPT-6 Astra , and GPT-6.2 Astra , plus an internal model at around 0.73. OpenAI has been feeding its models open math problems for more than a year. Starting with a model at about 0.76 log-perplexity, the models began producing breakthrough results, Pachocki writes. For researchers with a math background, he says, it was "deeply surreal" to watch solutions to longstanding questions pop up one after another in a single Slack thread. Those results include a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem , one of the Millennium Prize problems, though it hasn't been fully verified yet. The same goes for the proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis found by Claude and an Anthropic researcher. Pachocki thinks deep learning research itself could see something similar as soon as 2027, bringing a sudden avalanche of core advances in AI training. A footnote says the sharp acceleration in the chart starting in 2026 comes mostly from long-term research and compute investments and less from automation. Even so, AI itself has contributed major design work on OpenAI's latest models, according to the post. items.title: What to do when your WooCommerce store starts failing during Black Friday
items.desc: “Do I need to pay again?” Your customer sees an error at checkout. They don’t have an order confirmation, but you can see a successful charge ...
items.full: “Do I need to pay again?” Your customer sees an error at checkout. They don’t have an order confirmation, but you can see a successful charge in the payment dashboard. While you work out what to tell them, another message arrives about the same problem. Somebody on the team suggests restoring the morning backup. And that sounds reasonable enough at first until you remember the orders that come in after that point. Customers’ payments won’t disappear when you restore the database, but their order records just might. During Black Friday, you have to investigate with customers still at checkout. There isn’t always time to reproduce every failure before acting. Even so, a few checks can keep an urgent repair from making a bigger mess. We work through those decisions here, starting with whether customers can safely keep buying. The article then covers the symptoms you’re likely to encounter and how to choose a correction without losing track of payments already underway. A shared ticket or incident thread gives everyone somewhere to make note of the issues they’ve found. One person should coordinate production changes, though. This way, even if several people investigate, everybody is on the same page. Otherwise, your developer might roll back a plugin while a colleague changes its settings, and neither sees the store behave as expected. For the first few minutes, this is enough to work from: The first complaint may not be the first failure. New Relic’s 2025 retail research reports a median outage detection time of 30 minutes.
